identity.title: Spatial variations in Titan's atmospheric temperature: ALMA and Cassini comparisons from 2012 to 2015

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained public data of Titan from the ALMA science archive
We analyze data from four short ($\sim$3 minute) ALMA flux calibration observations of Titan

question.value: How does Titan's atmospheric temperature vary spatially and seasonally from 2012-2015, as retrieved from CO emission lines in ALMA flux-calibration data, and how does it compare with Cassini CIRS and radio occultation results?

evidence.quote: Here we present the first spatially resolved temperature measurements of Titan obtained using ground-based radio observations.
we extract spectra from 3 separate regions on Titan’s disk using datasets with beam sizes ranging from $0.35\times0.28''$ to $0.39\times0.34''$

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Public archival flux-calibration observations of Titan

evidence.quote: Titan is often used as a flux calibrator for ALMA science targets

provided.value: Nadir temperature maps (T84, T98, T100, T112) for a priori and comparison

evidence.quote: we elected to extract similar data from CIRS nadir maps taken during the T84, T98, T100, and T112 flybys of Titan

provided.value: Tropospheric temperature profiles for a priori and comparison

evidence.quote: Interpolating the HASI (cite: fulchignoni_05) and *Cassini* radio occultation science measurements from the T27, T31, T46, and T57 flybys

evidence.quote: We obtained spectral line parameters from the HITRAN 2012 and CDMS databases (cite: rothman_13; muller_01)

evidence.quote: We obtained initial flux density estimates by using the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 Titan flux model in the CASA reduction scripts

We re-ran these scripts in the NRAO’s CASA software package 4.7.0
Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 Titan flux model in the CASA reduction scripts, which is expected to be accurate to within 5$\%$

as described by (cite: teanby_13)

method.value: Modified JAO scripts in CASA, clean with Högbom, natural weighting, Doppler shift to Titan rest frame

evidence.quote: Image spectral coordinates were Doppler-shifted to Titan’s rest frame using Topocentric radial velocities from JPL Horizons ephemerides.
The image pixel sizes were set to 0.03$''\times$0.03$''$.

method.value: Extract flux over solid disk plus atmosphere plus 2-sigma_PSF; three regions North/Center/South with minimal beam overlap

evidence.quote: We chose to model spectra from 3 regions (hereafter referred to as ‘North’, ‘Center’, and ‘South’) chosen to be as independent as possible

key_parameters.value: Titan radius 2575 km plus 1200 km atmosphere

evidence.quote: extracting flux over Titan’s solid disk (2575 km), plus its extended atmosphere (1200 km)

method.value: Constant multiplicative scaling factor (<5%) per spectrum from offsets between data and model continuum, line wings and core

evidence.quote: A constant scaling factor was determined for each spectrum by averaging offsets between measurements of data and model continuum, CO line wings, and line core regions

validation.value: Scaling within errors of Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 model for CO lines

evidence.quote: ensured that flux density scaling factors were within the errors of the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 model for CO lines

method.value: NEMESIS line-by-line optimal estimation with 37-44 field-of-view averaging points; a priori from CIRS/Huygens, isothermal 160 K above 600 km

evidence.quote: Upper atmospheric temperatures (\>600 km) were held as isothermal at 160 K.

key_parameters.value: 5 K a priori errors, correlation length 1.5 scale heights

evidence.quote: with 5 K errors set on the *a priori* temperature profile; combined with a correlation length of 1.5 scale heights
with a constant CO abundance of 49.6 ppm as found by (cite: serigano_16)
We retrieve vertical temperature profiles by allowing NEMESIS to vary temperature measurements continuously throughout the atmosphere

validation.value: Comparison with CIRS and radio occultation

evidence.quote: To validate our model of Titan’s atmosphere and the retrieved temperature profiles

method.value: Use disk-averaged profiles as a priori; troposphere a priori from Cassini radio/HASI convolved with ALMA beam (2014, 2015)

evidence.quote: We proceeded to use disk-averaged measurements as *a priori* temperature profiles to model spatially resolved spectra

method.value: Two-sample KS test of retrieved profiles vs CIRS and radio occultation at <100 km

evidence.quote: applying a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test to the temperature profiles presented here
do not seem statistically significant (i.e. $\alpha$\>0.10)
We re-ran these scripts in the NRAO’s CASA software package 4.7.0
radiative transfer modeling using the Non-Linear Optimal Estimator for Multivariate Spectral Analysis (NEMESIS) software package in line-by-line mode

results_numeric.quantity: Stratopause (~320 km) warming in northern latitudes 2012-2015

evidence.quote: We measure the stratopause (320 km) to increase in temperature by 5 K in northern latitudes from 2012–2015
temperature profiles are found to consistently vary with latitude in all three years by up to 15 K

results_numeric.quantity: ALMA cooler than radio occultation, 50-100 km

evidence.quote: We obtain temperature profiles that are cooler than interpolated radio occultation measurements by up to 10 K

results_numeric.quantity: Largest temporal variation at ~120 km, north, 2012-2014

evidence.quote: We observe the largest temporal temperature variation of all profiles presented here, 7 K, from 2012–2014 at $\sim$ 120 km

findings_qualitative.value: Disk-averaged profiles are nearly constant 2012-2015, while spatially resolved regions show seasonal changes in stratosphere and mesosphere

evidence.quote: Disk-averaged temperature profiles stay relatively constant from year to year

claims.hypothesis: CO lines in ALMA flux-calibration data can retrieve spatially resolved temperature profiles consistent with Cassini
claims.experiment: NEMESIS retrievals for three regions compared to CIRS and radio occultation with KS tests
claims.finding: ALMA CO retrievals agree with Cassini within errors

evidence.quote: We find that deviations from *Cassini*/CIRS observations between 100–300 km and radio science measurements below 100 km are not statistically significant

claims.hypothesis: Seasonal variation is detectable in resolved regions
claims.result: ~5 K stratopause warming in north; lower stratosphere changes
claims.finding: Titan's atmosphere responds to season, mostly at high latitudes, though often within errors

evidence.quote: While temporal variations are often within the retrieved errors

why_this_data.value: Frequent public Titan flux-calibration observations over ALMA's lifetime

evidence.quote: allowing us to utilize frequent (almost daily for $\sim$7 months of the year) observations

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO abundances >20% from nominal gave poor fits or large temperature variations

evidence.quote: Temperature retrievals obtained using CO abundances in excess of $20\%$ of the nominal value (49.6 ppm) resulted in poor spectral fits or large variations in temperature

limitations_admitted.value: Short integration times and large beams limit temporal variation significance; latitudinal structure is dampened by beam weighting

evidence.quote: limited by the short integration times of flux calibration datasets and large beam sizes

referee_caveats_inferred: Ad hoc flux scaling factors (<5%) can shift retrieved temperatures and are not tabulated
Regional footprints span wide latitude ranges, limiting spatial claims
KS test on profiles is weakly justified for correlated profile points

data_public_as_stated.value: Public ALMA archive data; retrieved profiles and models posted online

evidence.quote: We obtained public data of Titan from the ALMA science archive
